gaps: Every maintained client is a library, not an agent-native CLI: python-garminconnect and garth expose Python objects, so an agent has to write a script per question.
No client keeps a local archive of the 28-day-capped daily-stats endpoints, so any multi-year question re-fetches the whole history every time.
GarminDB does keep a local database but is a batch importer with no query surface an agent can call, and no JSON output.
gccli is the only Go CLI and the only browser-loopback login, but it ships no local store and no cross-series analytics.
patterns: python-garminconnect: SSO service ticket exchanged at the DI OAuth2 token endpoint for a bearer plus refresh token, then plain refresh; no OAuth1 and no consumer key.
python-garminconnect: every daily-stats range request is chunked into 28-day windows and de-duplicated by calendar date.
garth: page size 28 for daily series and 52 for weekly series, encoded as a constant rather than discovered per call.
bpauli/gccli: loopback browser login on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port, so the tool never sees the password and never handles MFA or CAPTCHA.
GarminDB: a durable local store is what makes multi-year questions answerable at all.

novel_features.name: Loopback browser login with identity assertion
novel_features.description: Signs in through Garmin's own page in your browser, catches the redirect on a loopback port, and refuses to store a token whose account email does not match the one you named.
novel_features.rationale: Every other client either takes your password or scrapes a browser cookie; a shared browser session silently signs in the wrong household member, and only an identity check catches it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this once per Garmin account per home; after it, everything else works unattended from the refresh token.
novel_features.group: Auth you can trust with a household

novel_features.name: Windowed backfill of the 28-day-capped series
novel_features.description: Walks every daily-stats series backwards in 28-day windows into a local SQLite archive and resumes where it stopped.
novel_features.rationale: Garmin caps every daily-stats request at 28 days, so years of history exist only if something walks and stores them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this before any trend question; every analytics command reads the archive, not the API.

narrative.headline: Your whole Garmin history in a local database, not one 28-day page at a time.
narrative.value_prop: Garmin Connect caps every daily-stats request at 28 days and offers no personal API token, which is why the ecosystem is a handful of Python libraries rather than a tool you can call. This CLI signs in through your own browser, keeps each account's tokens in its own home, walks the whole history into SQLite, and answers sleep, training, heart-rate and activity questions from the archive with JSON on stdout.
narrative.auth_narrative: Garmin issues no personal API key. Sign-in goes through Garmin's own page in your browser: `auth login` opens it, catches the redirect back to a loopback port on 127.0.0.1, exchanges the ticket for an access token and a refresh token, and checks the account email on the resulting token against the one you named before writing anything to disk. The password never reaches this CLI, and the refresh token keeps the session alive without another browser visit. For a second household account, sign out of Garmin in the browser and run `auth login` again under that account's own GARMIN_HOME.

quickstart.comment: One browser sign-in; the email you pass is checked against the account that actually signed in.
Confirms the token works and prints the displayName the rest of the commands need.
Walks the 28-day-capped series into the local archive; the first run backfills, later runs are incremental.
A month of nightly sleep summaries straight from Garmin.

troubleshoots.symptom: `auth login` reports that the signed-in account does not match --email.
troubleshoots.fix: Another Garmin session owned the browser. Sign out of Garmin in the browser, then run `auth login` again; nothing was written to your home.

troubleshoots.symptom: Every wellness series comes back empty while activities are present.
troubleshoots.fix: The account has no wearable paired. Bike computers and trainers record activities but no sleep, heart-rate or body-battery series; check `daily-summary` for `includesWellnessData` before assuming a bug.

troubleshoots.symptom: A range longer than 28 days returns fewer rows than expected.
troubleshoots.fix: Garmin caps daily-stats requests at 28 calendar days. Use `sync` and query the local archive instead of asking one endpoint for a long range.

troubleshoots.symptom: Commands read the wrong person's data on a shared machine.
troubleshoots.fix: Set GARMIN_HOME (or pass --home) per account; `doctor --json` prints which home directory each kind resolved to and why.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI for any question about the owner's Garmin Connect history: sleep trends, training status and readiness, VO2 max, resting heart rate, step and intensity-minute trends, heart-rate zones, and the activity feed. It is at its best on questions that span months or years, because those are answered from the local archive rather than from Garmin's 28-day pages. Sync first, then query.
anti_triggers: Do not use it to write anything to Garmin Connect: every command is read-only.
Do not use it for another person's Garmin account without their own login in their own home.
Do not use it as a live device feed; data appears only after the watch or bike computer syncs to Garmin Connect.
Do not use it for Strava, Apple Health, Whoop or Oura data.

recipes.title: Time in zone for the last ride
recipes.command: garmin-pp-cli activities list --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.[0].activityId' | xargs garmin-pp-cli activities hr-time-in-zones
recipes.explanation: Zone seconds for one activity; pair it with `heart-rate zones` to label the zones.
